text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prince Hassan receives U.S. deputy secretary of state for trade and economic affairs. Prince says Jordan will stand against settling refugees. "We hope to review Jordan Rift Valley projects and 'fast track' scheme at Cairo economic summit."

- Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti chairs agriculture council meeting. Says 35 percent in savings on bread consumption, farmers' debts need restructuring and suggests setting up three bourses for agriculture and farm produce.
- Prince Hassan says we will rehabilitate all sectors of Jordanian society.

- Government slashes its share holdings in companies and hands the wheels over to the private sector. Thirty-one million government shares in four companies to be sold for over 100 million dinars and another offer to sell its shares in five firms. 14 international firms to meet in Amman to buy government shares in cement factory. Study to set up three bourses for vegetables and farm produce in the central valley, north and south of the country. $200 million to finance Jordanian imports from United States.
- Customs department to start implementing green light plan this month.
- Supply ministry regains control over prices.
- Prince Hassan stresses the need to open the Jordanian economy to the world. Prince hopes there will be a revival of the Middle East Development Bank and a definition of its plans and objectves.
- Kabariti says Jordan seeks to attract Arab and foreign funds.
- Kabariti says success of government's economic plan hinges on executing self-reliance plans.
- Subsidy move led to 35 percent cut in bread consumption - Kabariti. Prime Minister urges new agriculture policy and methods so as to achieve self-reliance.

- Regent: Jordan hopes to bolster ties with United States at public and private sector levels. Crown Prince meets American official, reaffirms Jordan rejects settling refugees because it would deprive them of their rights. Financing deal worth $200 million with Eximbank.
- Jordan determined to liberalise its economy and create right investment climate - premier.
